newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Laing picks nine stocks for 1997.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Laing picks nine stocks for 1997.

text.p: Strategists at Credit Lyonnais Laing on Monday named nine UK stocks that they expect to outperform the rest of the UK market during 1997.

In a research note, strategists said their main overweight stocks for the coming year were food and drink group Allied Domecq Plc, natural gas supplier British Gas Plc, telecoms group Cable & Wireless Plc, building materials group Caradon Plc, food manufacturer Hillsdown Holdings Plc, National Westminster Bank Plc, Royal Bank of Scotland Plc, supermarket group Safeway Plc and conglomerate Tomkins Plc.
The note said an outperformance of some 30 percent was expected from those nine during the year.
Laing also said its main "sell" recommendations were Williams Holdings Plc and British Sky Broadcasting Plc .
Laing said its main sector recommendations were for investors to be "overweight" in banks, building and construction stocks, building materials and merchants, and food retailers.
Conversely it was recommending an "underweight" position on the paper and packging, tobacco and engineering sectors.
The note said strengthening economic growth during 1997 would support the outperformance of "value-based" investing during the year, reversing the recent trend for "growth" stocks to outperform.
Sterling strength would favour stocks with high domestic exposure, it said, while cost-cutting would remain a key driver of growth in company profit margins.
The note said further consolidation was expected in the banking, aerospace, telecom and spirits sectors and that the outlook for the UK equity market as a whole was encouraging.
"While most of the risks associated with a Labour victory in strength of the economy should provide a favourable background for the market," the note said.
"A recovery in continental Europe should aid a resumption of manufacturing growth, despite the strength in sterling, with low raw material costs helping to improve margins."

Laing strategists also said institutional investors were flush with cash, having been building up liquidity ahead of the election which must be held by May 1997, providing another major bull case for UK equities.
Laing's target is for the FTSE 100 index to reach 4,450 by the end of 1997, some 350 points above its present level.
